news.title: Des Buckingham to lead All Whites through to the 2030 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: Former Wellington Phoenix and New Zealand age-group coach Des Buckingham has been named as the next head coach of the All Whites. Buckingham (41) will take up the role on July 1, 2027, and lead the national team through to the 2030 FIFA Men’s World Cup. He will also lead the national men’s U-23 team as they prepare for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. Buckingham is in his second season as head coach of Saudi Pro League club Al-Kholood and will complete his commitments there before joining NZ Football.

news.title: Amputee Football World Cup:: Black Challenge storm into Round of 16 with emphatic 6-0 rout of Iraq
news.lede: The Black Challenge delivered a stunning performance on Monday, thrashing Iraq 6-0 in their final Group D encounter to secure qualification for the round of 16 at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The two-time African champions produced a commanding display at Lucia II in San Juan de los Lagos, responding emphatically to their difficult start to the tournament with a convincing victory that kept their World Cup campaign alive. Stephen Richard Obeng’s men entered the decisive encounter under pressure after opening their campaign with a 2-0 defeat to former world champions Angola before settling for a 1-1 draw against Colombia on Sunday. However, the Black Challenge put those setbacks behind them in spectacular fashion, taking control of proceedings against their Middle Eastern opponents and showcasing their attacking quality with a six-goal performance.

news.title: Bellingham’s underwear ad highlights football’s growing US appeal
news.lede: The Calvin Klein billboard featuring Jude Bellingham overlooks one of the Big Apple's busiest shopping districts, drawing crowds of admirers. (AFP pic) NEW YORK: Football star Jude Bellingham has a trophy case of accolades to his name. But the England and Real Madrid attacking midfielder has been elevated to the pantheon of US pop culture immortality with his own extra-large Calvin Klein underwear billboard in Manhattan. Measuring 75 feet by 55 feet (22.9 by 16.8 meters), the giant billboard overlooking one of the Big Apple's busiest shopping havens has drawn crowds of admirers.
